scope: First qualification baselines for the five non-EmbeddingGemma engines on the Studio (Apple M2 Ultra, 192 GB, macOS). This records reproducible outputs and a contention-limited timing baseline; it is not a speed claim.

host.contention: Heavy unrelated agent load throughout (load average 16-30 on 24 logical CPUs); numbers are a floor/ceiling envelope, not a qualified latency.

build.features: qwen3 (dense candle); ONNX default for fastembed backends
build.binaries: engine_bench (dense) and new engine_aux_bench (sparse/M3/rerank), same commit

protocol.cases: scripts/parity/eg2_cases_text.json short suite (18 rows incl. ragged and reversed batch)
protocol.per_run: 3 warmups, 5 samples of >=200 ms each per case, medians
protocol.across_runs: 4 separate processes per engine; outputs compared exactly across all four
protocol.noise_control: none available on this host under current load; same-binary spread reported instead

verdict.exactness: PASS - SPLADE sparse indices/weights, BGE-M3 dense+sparse, rerank scores and order, ONNX dense bits and Qwen3 dense bits were identical across four independent processes per engine.
verdict.performance: PROVISIONAL - same-binary suite spread is 1.07x (Qwen3) to 1.69x (reranker) and worst-case per-case spread reaches 2.1x under load. No engine comparison or regression gate may be derived from this capture.
verdict.gate: Re-capture on a quiet host or admitted GPU before any performance statement, and keep these values only as the exactness baseline.

limits: Local Studio under heavy unrelated load; a busy host is not a benchmark host.
Short suite only; the t_long parity case, sparse support/weight preservation on long inputs, rerank tie stability and transport behaviour are not covered here.
Qwen3 ran on CPU with the candle backend; GPU/Metal variants and Apple-native Gemma runtimes remain unqualified.
No model, prompt, dtype or context change; no production install in this step.
